adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Germany (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: The page records that Saarland's state constitution was amended in 2011 so that its anti-discrimination provisions explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity, one of only five Lander constitutions to carry such a clause (Berlin since 1995, Brandenburg since 1992, Bremen since 2001, Saarland since 2011, Thuringia since 1993; Saxony-Anhalt in the public sector since 1997). It further records that Saarland, with Hesse, Berlin, Bremen and Schleswig-Holstein, tabled a joint Bundesrat motion for a ban on conversion therapy, presented in plenary on 12 April 2019, with Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia agreeing and Bavaria offering modified support. Gives the state-constitutional protection against discrimination on grounds of gender identity that a trans visitor stands under within Saarland.

adds.title: Transgender rights in Germany (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: The page states that hate speech on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity is not banned nationwide in Germany, but that some states have laws banning all forms of discrimination in their constitutions - Berlin, Brandenburg, Bremen, Saarland and Thuringia - and that in those states hate speech based on both sexual orientation and gender identity is prohibited. For Saarland this is a jurisdiction-specific enforcement difference: transphobic hate speech is prohibited under the state constitution, unlike in most of Germany, and the federal General Act on Equal Treatment (in force since 18 August 2006) bans discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, education, health services and the provision of goods and services.

adds.title: Jens Spahn will Pseudotherapien gegen Homosexualität verbieten
adds.summary: Zeit Online (10 April 2019) reports that parallel to Federal Health Minister Jens Spahn's announced plan to ban so-called conversion therapies, Hesse, Berlin, Bremen, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein planned to present a joint Bundesrat motion (Entschließungsantrag) for a ban that same week. Nails Saarland by name as one of the five tabling states in the run-up to the 12 April 2019 Bundesrat plenary presentation recorded by Wikipedia's LGBTQ rights in Germany page; the federal ban was subsequently approved by the Bundestag on 7 May 2020.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Germany (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: The page records that Schleswig-Holstein, with Hesse, Berlin, Bremen and Saarland, tabled a joint motion in the Bundesrat for a ban on conversion therapy, presented in plenary on 12 April 2019; Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia agreed to the motion, Bavaria expressed potential support with modifications, and the federal ban was approved by the Bundestag on 7 May 2020 with support from all parties except the AfD. Documents the state government's concrete action in the federal conversion-therapy ban campaign in a record where no SH-specific trans statute or ordinance survives.

Fixes Schleswig-Holstein by name as one of the five tabling states in the run-up to the 12 April 2019 Bundesrat plenary presentation recorded by Wikipedia's LGBTQ rights in Germany page.
